current_activity: strikes toward the Zon bridge to cut the Market Garden corridor; nearly takes the 101st Airborne command post
notes: Event date: late afternoon of 19 September 1944 (D plus 2) (MacDonald, chs. 7 and 8). Event definition: Rerouted from Aachen to the First Parachute Army, the brigade strikes toward Zon late on 19 September to sever the corridor of the British ground column; the 101st Airborne Division command post and the Bailey bridge at Zon almost fall (MacDonald, chs. 7 and 8; Wikipedia). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 7, p. 153: "It was Major von Maltzahn's 107th Panzer Brigade that on D-Day had been rerouted from Aachen to the assistance of the First Parachute Army"; MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 8, p. 187: "his command post and the Bailey bridge over the Wilhelmina Canal at Zon had almost fallen to the first strike of the 107th Panzer Brigade"; Wikipedia, List of German brigades in World War II: "the brigade was sent to assist the German response against the Allied paradrops of Operation Market Garden". Location: Son, Noord-Brabant (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: MacDonald names Zon (Son). Commander: Major Freiherr von Maltzahn (MacDonald, ch. 7). Opponents: US 101st Airborne Division.

current_activity: with Kampfgruppe Walther, cuts Hell's Highway between Veghel and Uden and turns toward Veghel
notes: Event date: 22 September 1944 (MacDonald, ch. 8). Event definition: Leading Kampfgruppe Walther, the tanks of the brigade cut the corridor between Veghel and Uden and turn down the highway toward Veghel (MacDonald, ch. 8). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 8, p. 189: "Kampfgruppe Walther with tanks of the 107th Panzer Brigade in the lead readily cut Hell's Highway between Veghel and Uden". Location: Veghel, Noord-Brabant, Netherlands with a precision of 3 km. Location support: MacDonald names Veghel and Uden. Commander: Major Freiherr von Maltzahn (MacDonald, ch. 7). Opponents: US 101st Airborne Division. Context: Kampfgruppe Walther is not a unit in the dataset; the row keeps the First Parachute Army relation.

current_activity: with Kampfgruppe Walther, uses its tanks as antitank guns before Overloon against the US 7th Armored Division
notes: Event date: 30 September to 2 October 1944 (MacDonald, ch. 10). Event definition: Pulled back into the LXXXVI Corps sector, Kampfgruppe Walther, whose main component is still the brigade (about seven Mark IVs and twenty Panthers), defends Overloon, using the tanks mainly as antitank guns from concealed positions; fourteen American tanks are knocked out (MacDonald, ch. 10). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 10, p. 236: "The major component still was the 107th Panzer Brigade"; MacDonald, The Siegfried Line Campaign, ch. 10, p. 239: "Employing the tanks of the 107th Panzer Brigade primarily in antitank roles from concealed positions"; Wikipedia, List of German brigades in World War II: "Placed under LXXXVI Corps". Location: Overloon, Noord-Brabant (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: MacDonald names Overloon. Commander: Major Freiherr von Maltzahn (MacDonald, ch. 7). Opponents: US 7th Armored Division.
